craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta as paradox held; vyabhicāri wonder at incompatibles held (C1 rasa block). Sanskrit-first: siddhaṃ akāryam (ESTABLISHED yet uneffectable — siddha kept against akārya, no smoothing); anīśa īśa (NO-LORD yet LORD — kept paired); stauti (I PRAISE — the verb IS the verse's end). Rows: 9 (paradox pairs kept paired, never resolved — established/uneffected, no-lord/yet-lord), 7 (‘Bhairava, Lord’ vocative before the praise-verb — address then act), 1 (‘I praise’ closes — after all doctrine, the act). Close: ‘I praise’. Rupture: semicolon before ‘the self, no lord’ (metaphysics turns to self-naming). Rejected: ‘lord beyond lordship’ — killed: smoothing kills the paradox (Bar 6: never smooth); ‘I sing’ — killed: stauti is praise-speech, song would name the medium. Read aloud: THUS — SELF-con-SCIOUS-ness … NEV-er to be ef-FECT-ed; NO-lord AND-yet-LORD … BHAI-ra-va, LORD, i-PRAISE.

lines: Thus — self-consciousness, established from the first, never to be effected; the self, no lord and yet lord;
whose place and time are full of its own power — eternal, pervasive: Bhairava, Lord, I praise.
l4.sanskrit_cite: itthaṃ svasaṃvedanam ādisiddham asādhyam ātmānam anīśam īśam | svaśaktisaṃpūrṇavadeśakālaṃ nityaṃ vibhuṃ bhairavanātham īḍe
